pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/core/chat_turn.rs:484 a follow-up sent while the session's previous run is still going is neither injected additively nor refused/queued: it starts a second run resuming the stored Claude session id, which finish() only advances at :665 when the first run completes, so the new turn forks from turn N-1 and never sees turn N; the last finisher's session id then wins the next --resume. The phone chat_send reaches this same door with no UI guard

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/core/chat_turn.rs:484 turn input built from the last COMPLETED turn's session id with no in-flight check; neither the earliest-safe-point injection nor the technique's own fallback (refuse mid-unit input and queue visibly at the surface) is realized, so concurrent turns silently fork the conversation

src-tauri/src/commands/core/chat_turn.rs:615 a run that is not completed (incl. restart-classified incomplete) writes no authoritative reply; the user row links its run, so the indeterminate status stays on the execution row rather than being re-encoded as a failure
src-tauri/src/commands/core/chat_turn.rs:540 the turn starts a top-level persona run through execute_persona_inner; no run is launched from inside a run here

pairs.registryProposal: additive-input-at-the-call-boundary assumes one in-process loop; a CLI-per-turn runtime (each turn a fresh process resuming a stored session id) has no model-call boundary to inject at, so the only conformant shapes are the refuse/queue fallback or serialising turns per session. A sentence naming that topology (and that the stored resume pointer is the race) would let judges route it without inference.
